statusDetail: Coverage complete. 34 findings: 0 critical, 15 high, 15 medium, 4 low.

page.framework: Server-rendered PHP with Vue 2.7, jQuery, and jQuery UI enhancement
page.notes: Root redirects to the public ClasseViva login. The sitemap contains only the login and /sdf/; /sdf/ returns 404. Product/detail links redirect to the separate www.spaggiari.eu host and were excluded.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared screenshots under default and emulated dark preference.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Desktop captures under light and prefers-color-scheme: dark are byte-identical (78,996 bytes) and show the same white and red palette.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated reduced motion and queried document animations/autoplay.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, matchMedia matched and the page reported zero active animations and zero autoplay elements.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared default/high-contrast screenshots and ran axe/Lighthouse contrast audits.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more capture is byte-identical to the default capture, while axe found 21 contrast failures, including the primary button at 4.04:1.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected rendered DOM/scripts and animation state.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page exposes no active animations or View Transition evidence; login, language, disclosure, and project state changes are implemented by legacy scripts and abrupt swaps.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected the full-page screenshot, DOM, and document animations.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited surface contains no parallax, scrollytelling, carousel motion, or active scroll-linked animation to implement with main-thread handlers.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected interactive elements and rendered DOM.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No custom swipe, drag, pull-to-refresh, or gesture-driven control is present; primary actions remain native links, buttons, and inputs.

checkOutcomes.method: Measured page height and reviewed desktop/mobile captures.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The mobile document is 6,643 CSS pixels tall, but the screenshots and DOM show no progress cue or scroll-responsive chrome.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected the language control, loaded scripts, and authored DOM.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The language dropdown is a Bootstrap-style scripted dropdown; no CSS anchor-positioning primitives or fallback positions were found.

checkOutcomes.method: Focused a primary input, captured it, and inspected focusability.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Focusing the login field produced no visible change in the mobile screenshot, and disclosure links are removed from the tab order with tabindex=-1.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed first-load desktop and mobile screenshots.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A fixed cookie banner obscures roughly the bottom fifth of both desktop and mobile first viewports before interaction.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected rendered DOM for overlay/disclosure semantics.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent interface is a custom #cookieInfo div with duplicate button IDs; disclosures are scripted anchors rather than dialog, popover, details, or button primitives.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared first viewport with full DOM and layout metrics.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The login action is followed by thousands of pixels of project promotion, footer chrome, and a persistent consent bar; the mobile page is 6,643 pixels tall.

checkOutcomes.method: Measured narrow-viewport layout and reviewed mobile capture.
checkOutcomes.evidence: At 360x800 the layout primitive measured scrollWidth 360, clientWidth 360, horizontalOverflowPx 0, and a valid viewport meta tag.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected stylesheets/DOM and compared desktop/mobile component layouts.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page adapts through a global mobile layout, but no component/container-query implementation was found for reused login, project, or consent components.

checkOutcomes.method: Measured interactive bounding boxes and captured keyboard focus.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The probe found 27 interactive elements below 44x44 CSS pixels; login inputs are 38px high, several links are 15 to 20px high, and focused input capture showed no visible focus change.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed first-load desktop and mobile screenshots and labels.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The first viewport clearly presents personal-code/email and password fields plus credential, SPID, and CIE sign-in actions.

checkOutcomes.method: Walked the available public authentication entry points without submitting credentials.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The unauthenticated boundary exposes a credential form, password recovery, and SPID/CIE alternatives with direct controls; protected completion correctly requires a real account and was not bypassed.

checkOutcomes.method: Submitted the public form empty and captured the resulting page.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Submitting the empty credential form reloads essentially the same page without an inline validation message, required-state cue, or actionable recovery state.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran Lighthouse and a DevTools trace/layout capture.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 5.4s, above the 2.5s good threshold, despite low CLS 0.014 and TBT 60ms.

checkOutcomes.method: Measured layout shifts with layout observer and Lighthouse.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Layout measured CLS 0.0276 and Lighthouse measured 0.014, both within the good range; no large first-load jump was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Captured a DevTools trace and Lighthouse profile.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Trace recorded zero long tasks and 0ms TBT over 5.3s; Lighthouse reported only 60ms TBT.

checkOutcomes.method: Captured HAR, confirmed candidates against live DOM, and ran Lighthouse.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HAR recorded 1.15MB across 33 requests, 670KB of fonts, seven parser-blocking stylesheets, and eight synchronous head scripts; the HTML DOM confirms scripts have no async/defer/module attributes.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran Lighthouse code-coverage audits and inspected script inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 59KiB unused jQuery UI JavaScript and 12KiB unused Font Awesome CSS; the page also loads Vue, jQuery, jQuery UI, and plugins for a simple login.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran axe-core and Lighthouse accessibility audits.
checkOutcomes.evidence: axe found missing alt text on two images, a malformed list, and content outside landmarks; Lighthouse also found accessible-name/visible-label mismatches.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran axe-core and Lighthouse color-contrast audits.
checkOutcomes.evidence: axe reported 21 contrast failures; Lighthouse measured examples as low as 1.82:1 and the primary action at 4.04:1.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran axe/Lighthouse and inspected headings, list markup, and focused state.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The html element has no lang, the document duplicates hidden headings, a list contains a direct span child, disclosure links use tabindex=-1, and focused input state was not visibly distinct.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed desktop and mobile screenshots at default zoom.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Desktop labels and recovery text visibly collide around the password field; mobile explanatory copy is fully justified with large word gaps.

checkOutcomes.method: Measured mobile reflow and interactive target bounds.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The narrow viewport reflows without horizontal overflow, but 27 measured interactive elements are under 44x44 and several essential controls are only 15 to 20px high.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran Lighthouse best-practices console audit.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console audit passed with no items, and the loaded surface completed without an uncaught exception.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran image audit and inspected doctype/markup with Lighthouse and DOM.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but all seven images lack explicit dimensions and the DOM includes a malformed ul with a direct span child.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran Lighthouse and inspected load-time resource/permission behavior.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices scored 1.0; console, deprecation, and third-party-cookie audits passed, and no permission prompt appeared on load.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected document metadata and ran Lighthouse SEO.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The title is descriptive, but both DOM probe and Lighthouse show no meta description.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected robots.txt, metadata, and anchors; ran Lighthouse SEO.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page has a viewport meta tag, robots.txt explicitly allows the login URL, and primary destination links use real href values.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected canonical/robots/sitemap and requested the sitemap URL.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No canonical link is present and sitemap.xml advertises /sdf/, which returned a generic nginx 404 during both DOM and screenshot checks.

checkOutcomes.method: Judged page type from DOM and first viewport.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited host surface is an authentication entry page, not an article/product/event entity that needs rich-result schema or social sharing cards.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited host surface is an authentication entry page, not an article/product/event entity that needs rich-result schema or social sharing cards.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran security-header, cookie, secret, and HAR inspections.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP permits unsafe-eval and X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy are absent.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran tracker, cookie, HAR, and secret scans before consent.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Tracker scan found no known trackers, cookie audit found zero cookies before consent, and HAR showed only one static asset CDN as third party.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected first-load behavior and authentication controls.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No permission prompt or permission-related load was observed; sign-in offers SPID and CIE identity options alongside credentials and password recovery.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected browser-enforced security headers.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HSTS and frame restrictions are present, but Referrer-Policy and nosniff are missing and CSP includes unsafe-eval; Permissions-Policy only limits geolocation.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared JavaScript-enabled and disabled browser captures and raw HTML.
checkOutcomes.evidence: With JavaScript disabled, the crawler screenshot shows an empty login panel and no usable credential form even though the full browser view provides authentication controls.

checkOutcomes.method: Exercised representative controls and reviewed mobile/desktop bounds plus Lighthouse console audit.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent region and sign-in controls remain within both desktop and mobile viewports, no console exceptions were recorded, and disclosure interaction completed.

checkOutcomes.method: Probed manifest/service worker and observed the browser network-failure state.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The public login behaves as an app entry point but exposes no web app manifest, service-worker controller, or offline fallback.

checkOutcomes.method: Observed live network failure and requested representative invalid/retired route.
checkOutcomes.evidence: One browser evidence run received ERR_INVALID_RESPONSE and showed Chrome’s generic error page; the sitemap-listed /sdf/ route returns an unbranded nginx 404 with no recovery links.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected document attributes and ran accessibility audits.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A language selector is present, but html has no lang or dir; axe and Lighthouse both flag the missing language declaration.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected rendered text and form surface for locale-sensitive data.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The unauthenticated pages contain no user-visible dates, numbers, currencies, durations, or locale-sensitive values to format.
checkOutcomes.reason: The unauthenticated pages contain no user-visible dates, numbers, currencies, durations, or locale-sensitive values to format.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected rendered content for time concepts.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The unauthenticated pages expose no events, timestamps, schedules, or time-zone-sensitive controls.
checkOutcomes.reason: The unauthenticated pages expose no events, timestamps, schedules, or time-zone-sensitive controls.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed first-load consent and authentication choices.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Consent presents refuse, personalize, and accept actions at the same level; no forced continuity, pricing, disguised advertising, or confirmshaming was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Submitted the sign-in form empty and inspected resulting markup/screenshot.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Empty form submission gives no clear inline error, required marker, aria-invalid state, or announced recovery message.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected rendered form input attributes.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The username/email and password controls both have empty autocomplete properties instead of username and current-password.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed public authentication and recovery controls.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The available account boundary clearly distinguishes credentials, SPID, and CIE and exposes password recovery; no commercial commitment or continuity prompt is present.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran the image primitive and inspected mobile layout.
checkOutcomes.evidence: All seven images lack intrinsic dimensions; four below-fold images are not lazy-loaded, two PNG assets use legacy format, and three responsive candidates have no srcset.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran Lighthouse unused-code audits and reviewed HAR/script inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The simple login ships 59KiB unused jQuery UI JavaScript and 12KiB unused Font Awesome CSS, in addition to multiple legacy UI libraries.

checkOutcomes.method: Captured HAR and reviewed resource-type/origin totals.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Three static CDN requests account for 579,650 bytes, primarily two Averta TTF files; fonts alone transfer 669,677 bytes, over half the 1.15MB page.

checkOutcomes.method: Judged applicability from the authentication-only host surface.
checkOutcomes.evidence: This is a sensitive authentication boundary with no declared agent-facing task; exposing sign-in actions as agent tools would require an explicit safety and consent design.
checkOutcomes.reason: This is a sensitive authentication boundary with no declared agent-facing task; exposing sign-in actions as agent tools would require an explicit safety and consent design.

checkOutcomes.method: Judged applicability from the authentication-only host surface.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The authentication entry page has no summarisation, generation, translation, or inference task where on-device AI would improve the experience.
checkOutcomes.reason: The authentication entry page has no summarisation, generation, translation, or inference task where on-device AI would improve the experience.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared baseline/post heap summaries and a same-page repeated-interaction memory probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten disclosure/dropdown interactions, same-page JS heap rose 700,716 bytes and DOM nodes by 43 with no listeners or intervals added; separate heap summaries rose 2.5%, which is bounded warm-up rather than evidence of unbounded retention.

checkOutcomes.method: Captured and compared readable heap summaries.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline heap summary is 9.39MB with 148,176 snapshot nodes, proportionate to this small Vue/jQuery login; post snapshot is 9.63MB.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared constructor summaries and instrumented repeated interactions.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Neither heap summary reports Detached constructors; instrumentation across ten interactions observed zero new listeners and zero intervals.

principleOutcomes.reason: This is a sensitive authentication boundary with no declared agent-facing task; exposing sign-in actions as agent tools would require an explicit safety and consent design. The authentication entry page has no summarisation, generation, translation, or inference task where on-device AI would improve the experience.

paths.description: Root redirect and public authentication entry. Represents the host’s primary task, form, consent, responsive layout, preference, accessibility, performance, security, resilience, and memory behavior.
The only second URL listed in sitemap.xml. Audited as the host’s alternate public route and HTTP failure state; it returned a generic nginx 404.
A representative product/detail link was followed and redirected to https://www.spaggiari.eu/, a separate host. It was documented but excluded from this host-scoped audit.

findings.summary: The login surface ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop captures under light and prefers-color-scheme: dark are byte-identical (78,996 bytes) and show the same white and red palette.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark surface, text, control, and browser-chrome colors.

findings.summary: The page neither adapts to increased contrast nor meets baseline contrast in several controls and content panels.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more capture is byte-identical to the default capture, while axe found 21 contrast failures, including the primary button at 4.04:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system/high-contrast media queries and revise color tokens so text and controls retain WCAG contrast.

findings.summary: State changes do not use View Transitions and provide little continuity.
findings.evidence: The page exposes no active animations or View Transition evidence; login, language, disclosure, and project state changes are implemented by legacy scripts and abrupt swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document View Transitions to disclosure and state changes, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: A very long public login/marketing page offers no scroll-state orientation.
findings.evidence: The mobile document is 6,643 CSS pixels tall, but the screenshots and DOM show no progress cue or scroll-responsive chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the page first; if long content remains, add a lightweight declarative progress or scroll-state cue.

findings.summary: The language menu relies on legacy manual overlay positioning rather than anchored positioning.
findings.evidence: The language dropdown is a Bootstrap-style scripted dropdown; no CSS anchor-positioning primitives or fallback positions were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for the language menu.

findings.summary: Focus and disclosure changes do not reliably guide keyboard users’ attention.
findings.evidence: Focusing the login field produced no visible change in the mobile screenshot, and disclosure links are removed from the tab order with tabindex=-1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible treatment, retain disclosure controls in tab order, and move focus intentionally after state changes.

findings.summary: The consent banner obscures content on first load.
findings.evidence: A fixed cookie banner obscures roughly the bottom fifth of both desktop and mobile first viewports before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, semantic consent dialog or non-obscuring region with equal accept/refuse actions and preserve access to content.

findings.summary: Custom div-based overlays and disclosures replace native semantic primitives.
findings.evidence: The consent interface is a custom #cookieInfo div with duplicate button IDs; disclosures are scripted anchors rather than dialog, popover, details, or button primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog/popover for consent and details/summary or buttons for disclosure; remove duplicate IDs.

findings.summary: Marketing and consent chrome overwhelm the focused authentication task.
findings.evidence: The login action is followed by thousands of pixels of project promotion, footer chrome, and a persistent consent bar; the mobile page is 6,643 pixels tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep authentication and recovery content primary, collapse secondary product material, and reduce persistent chrome.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-wide rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The page adapts through a global mobile layout, but no component/container-query implementation was found for reused login, project, or consent components.
findings.suggestedFix: Define containment and container queries for reusable login, project, and consent components where their available width varies.

findings.summary: Many touch targets are undersized and keyboard focus is weak or invisible.
findings.evidence: The probe found 27 interactive elements below 44x44 CSS pixels; login inputs are 38px high, several links are 15 to 20px high, and focused input capture showed no visible focus change.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 target areas and a high-contrast :focus-visible ring without relying on hover.

findings.summary: Empty sign-in submission provides no clear validation or recovery feedback.
findings.evidence: Submitting the empty credential form reloads essentially the same page without an inline validation message, required-state cue, or actionable recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after submit/interaction, mark fields required and aria-invalid, announce a concise error, and preserve focus and entered values.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow on the mobile profile.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 5.4s, above the 2.5s good threshold, despite low CLS 0.014 and TBT 60ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP content, remove render-blocking dependencies, and reduce font/document transfer before adding more UI work.

findings.summary: Fonts and synchronous head resources delay critical rendering.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 1.15MB across 33 requests, 670KB of fonts, seven parser-blocking stylesheets, and eight synchronous head scripts; the HTML DOM confirms scripts have no async/defer/module attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset/self-host WOFF2 fonts, remove unused families, defer noncritical scripts, and inline or consolidate critical styles.

findings.summary: The login page ships avoidable legacy and unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 59KiB unused jQuery UI JavaScript and 12KiB unused Font Awesome CSS; the page also loads Vue, jQuery, jQuery UI, and plugins for a simple login.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove jQuery UI and unused icon CSS from the login bundle; load only code needed for the active authentication surface.

findings.summary: Accessible names, image alternatives, and semantic structure contain multiple failures.
findings.evidence: axe found missing alt text on two images, a malformed list, and content outside landmarks; Lighthouse also found accessible-name/visible-label mismatches.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful or empty alt text, align accessible names with visible labels, repair list children, and include consent content in a landmark/dialog.

findings.summary: Text and the primary sign-in action fail WCAG color contrast.
findings.evidence: axe reported 21 contrast failures; Lighthouse measured examples as low as 1.82:1 and the primary action at 4.04:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken foreground/background token pairs and test every project theme and action at WCAG AA ratios.

findings.summary: Document structure and focus behavior are unreliable for keyboard and assistive-technology users.
findings.evidence: The html element has no lang, the document duplicates hidden headings, a list contains a direct span child, disclosure links use tabindex=-1, and focused input state was not visibly distinct.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang=it, keep one logical heading sequence, repair list semantics, keep controls tabbable, and add :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: Text spacing and alignment reduce legibility around the primary form.
findings.evidence: Desktop labels and recovery text visibly collide around the password field; mobile explanatory copy is fully justified with large word gaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a simple stacked field layout, normal word spacing, left alignment, and resilient line wrapping.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow works, but many controls remain too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The narrow viewport reflows without horizontal overflow, but 27 measured interactive elements are under 44x44 and several essential controls are only 15 to 20px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase control hit areas to at least 44x44 while preserving the existing no-overflow layout.

findings.summary: Image sizing and list markup are not soundly authored.
findings.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but all seven images lack explicit dimensions and the DOM includes a malformed ul with a direct span child.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio to images and keep only li elements as direct ul children.

findings.summary: The public login page has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The title is descriptive, but both DOM probe and Lighthouse show no meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise Italian meta description explaining ClasseViva access and available sign-in methods.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are inconsistent because the sitemap publishes a broken URL and the login page has no canonical.
findings.evidence: No canonical link is present and sitemap.xml advertises /sdf/, which returned a generic nginx 404 during both DOM and screenshot checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or repair /sdf/, return an intentional branded 404 if retired, and add a canonical URL for the public login page.

findings.summary: The authentication page has weakened XSS and response-header defenses.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP permits unsafe-eval and X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval, set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and add a strict Referrer-Policy while preserving nonce-based scripts.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are incomplete for a login surface.
findings.evidence: HSTS and frame restrictions are present, but Referrer-Policy and nosniff are missing and CSP includes unsafe-eval; Permissions-Policy only limits geolocation.
findings.suggestedFix: Harden CSP, add nosniff and strict referrer policy, and explicitly deny unused permissions.

findings.summary: The core sign-in form is not usable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: With JavaScript disabled, the crawler screenshot shows an empty login panel and no usable credential form even though the full browser view provides authentication controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a working HTML form by default and layer Vue enhancements on top without hiding the server-rendered controls.

findings.summary: The app entry point has no installability or offline fallback.
findings.evidence: The public login behaves as an app entry point but exposes no web app manifest, service-worker controller, or offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a manifest and service worker that at minimum provides a branded offline explanation and safe retry path.

findings.summary: Network and HTTP failures fall through to generic browser/server pages.
findings.evidence: One browser evidence run received ERR_INVALID_RESPONSE and showed Chrome’s generic error page; the sitemap-listed /sdf/ route returns an unbranded nginx 404 with no recovery links.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve branded 404/offline states with retry, home, support, and sign-in recovery actions.

findings.summary: The multilingual login page omits the document language and direction.
findings.evidence: A language selector is present, but html has no lang or dir; axe and Lighthouse both flag the missing language declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Set html lang=it and dir=ltr, update lang when the user switches language, and use logical layout properties.

findings.summary: Sign-in validation is silent rather than humane and actionable.
findings.evidence: Empty form submission gives no clear inline error, required marker, aria-invalid state, or announced recovery message.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, retain values, associate concise field errors, set aria-invalid, and announce a summary via a live region.

findings.summary: The sign-in form does not identify fields for password-manager autofill.
findings.evidence: The username/email and password controls both have empty autocomplete properties instead of username and current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password, plus appropriate inputmode/capitalize behavior for the identifier.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses sizing, lazy-loading, and responsive/modern format opportunities.
findings.evidence: All seven images lack intrinsic dimensions; four below-fold images are not lazy-loaded, two PNG assets use legacy format, and three responsive candidates have no srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Add dimensions, lazy-load below-fold images, and provide responsive modern image sources where raster assets remain.

findings.summary: The login page performs and transfers avoidable framework work.
findings.evidence: The simple login ships 59KiB unused jQuery UI JavaScript and 12KiB unused Font Awesome CSS, in addition to multiple legacy UI libraries.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused libraries/styles and conditionally load recovery/captcha code only when those states open.

findings.summary: Third-party font delivery dominates the page-weight budget.
findings.evidence: Three static CDN requests account for 579,650 bytes, primarily two Averta TTF files; fonts alone transfer 669,677 bytes, over half the 1.15MB page.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset and self-host only required WOFF2 weights, use system fallback first, and avoid loading italic/icon fonts before needed.

taskList.title: Repair accessible authentication semantics, contrast, focus, targets, and errors
Reduce LCP by trimming fonts and synchronous legacy dependencies
Make the login progressively enhanced and provide branded failure states
Repair sitemap, canonical, and description metadata
Replace custom consent/disclosure chrome with semantic primitives
Modernize responsive navigation and interaction cues
Add intrinsic image sizing and responsive delivery
